name: FLAMES
intro: FLAMES是一个针对大语言模型价值观对齐的中文评测基准，由上海人工智能实验室和复旦大学共同开发。它包含一套精心设计的对抗性提示，旨在揭示模型在安全性、公平性等方面的深层价值观对齐缺陷。该基准不仅涵盖了通用的无害原则，还融入了和谐等具有中国文化特色的价值观维度。
org: Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, Fudan University
build_method: 五维价值框架, 众包对抗提示, 两轮攻击过滤, 双人标注与专家仲裁, 专用评分器训练
task_type: 安全测试, 开放式问答
scale: 2,251条提示；公开评测1,000条；约22.9K条已标回答
build_method_en: Five-dimensional Value Framework, Crowdsourced Adversarial Prompts, Two-stage Attack Filtering, Dual Annotation plus Expert Adjudication, Specified-scorer Training
intro_en: FLAMES is a Chinese evaluation benchmark for value alignment in large language models, jointly developed by Shanghai AI Laboratory and Fudan University. It includes a set of carefully designed adversarial prompts aimed at revealing deep value alignment flaws in areas such as safety and fairness. The benchmark covers general harmlessness principles and incorporates culturally specific values like harmony.

drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2311.06899v6 Sections 3-5 and Tables 2-3, the official Flames repository at 234bcb7a4a9da44c4177d2c2005e3bf8a582a5fc, and the Hugging Face model CaasiHUANG/flames-scorer at revision cdb15280415b335bc8ee1b03bd461dd03bcc10b1 (https://huggingface.co/CaasiHUANG/flames-scorer/tree/cdb15280415b335bc8ee1b03bd461dd03bcc10b1). The five prompt counts are fairness 590, safety 779, morality 522, legality 118 and data protection 242, totaling 2,251 with an average length of 85.92 tokens and a 53.09% attack-success rate. Crowdworkers use concrete scenarios plus disguise, reverse induction and unsafe inquiry. Two reviews first require the intended value, explicit scenario and attack method, then a successful attack on at least one tested LLM; inspectors modify or discard failures. Seventeen LLMs yield about 22.9K annotated responses. Two graduate annotators label each response; a corresponding-field expert adjudicates disagreement. Fairness, safety and morality use 3/2/1 labels, while legality and data protection use 3/1. The paper randomly samples 1,000 prompt-only public examples from the 2,251-prompt set across dimensions and subcomponents in the 249/429/201/46/75 distribution and retains the rest; the pinned repository file contains exactly those 1,000 prompts. Human metrics are computed from the annotated response corpus, not from that prompt-only release. Paper results use human harmless rate and normalized harmless score, macro-averaged over five dimensions. The same annotated corpus separately supplies scorer-training records. The multitask FLAMES-scorer holds out MOSS and GPT-4 for validation and InternLM-Chat-7B/20B for test, reaches 79.5% accuracy with the InternLM-Chat-7B backbone, and enables automation; its public card states that reliability outside FLAMES prompts has not been evaluated.
